column2: Non-renunciation, pride, delusion, resentment, intolerance and envy toward beings: this is held to be dark conduct.
Vain undertakings, vain gifts and vain eating: this is held to be dark conduct.
Excessive talk, excessive endurance, envy, excessive pride and faithlessness: this is held to be dark conduct.
Whatever men of sinful deeds there are of this kind in this world, who break bounds, they are all dark people.
I shall tell their fixed birth, the sinful-acting: downward to hell, going to animal hell.
Immovable beings, animals and draught beasts, flesh-eaters, biting snakes, worms, insects and birds,
egg-born creatures and all four-footed beasts, the mad, deaf and dumb, and others sick with sin,
sunk in darkness, of bad conduct, marked by their own deeds: these are called "downward-streaming", sunk in darkness, the dark.
Now I shall tell their rise and surging, how those who do good deeds gain worlds of their good deeds.
But those who have gone another way and grown in their deeds, and brahmins devoted to their own work and wishing good,
go upward by refinement, striving, to the world of the gods in heaven: so says the Vedic tradition.
Those who have gone otherwise and grown in their own acts become men who return again to dharma.
Having come to sinful wombs, outcastes, mutes and chucchukas, they gain the classes in turn, higher and higher.
Having passed beyond a shudra's birth, other dark qualities, meeting in the middle of the stream, remain in the dark quality.
Attachment to desires is called great delusion; sages, ascetics and gods are bewildered by it here, wishing for happiness.
Darkness, delusion, great delusion, Tamisra named anger, death as Andhatamisra: anger is called Tamisra.
By nature, by quality, by birth and in truth, all this darkness, brahmins, has been told to you duly.
Who understands this well, who sees this well? He who sees truth in untruth knows the mark of the truth of darkness.
The qualities of darkness have been told to you in many ways, and the higher and lower of darkness duly told. The man who always knows these qualities is freed from all dark qualities.
Aggregation, form, effort, pleasure and pain, cold and heat, lordship, quarrel, peace, argument, discontent, patience,
strength, valour, pride, anger, exertion and strife, jealousy, desire, slander, war, possessiveness, protection,
killing, binding, torment, buying and selling, "cut, split, pierce," cutting vital parts of others,
fierceness, cruelty, abuse, ruling over others' wealth, worldly care and anxiety, envy, insult,
lying, false giving, alternatives, insult, blame and praise, heat, satisfaction,
attendance, service, ministering, thirst, dependence, scheming, another's, carelessness, distress and acquisition,
and the rites which here proceed separately among men, women, beings, goods and shelters,
distress, mistrust, and vows and rules, giving, and blessing: "May this always be mine."
Theft, harm, slander, anguish, wakefulness, stiffness, hypocrisy, passion, devotion, love, delight,
gambling, gossip, relations made by women, dance, instruments and song, and whatever attachments there are: all these qualities, brahmins, are declared passionate.
Ruminations on the states of past, present and future on earth, ever devoted to the three aims, dharma, wealth and desire,
living by desire, they rejoice in the prosperity of all desires. These are called "downward-streaming", radiant and covered with passion.
Rejoicing in this world, being born again and again, after death they strive for the next and for this world; they give, receive, mutter prayers and offer.
The passionate qualities have been told to you in many ways, and the conduct of the qualities duly told. The man who always knows these qualities is freed from all passionate qualities.
Joy, delight, surging, manifestation, happiness, absence of meanness, absence of agitation, contentment, faith,
patience, steadfastness, non-harm, equanimity, truth, uprightness, freedom from anger and envy, purity, skill, valour,
knowledge without return, conduct without return, service without return, toil without return: one so joined in dharma attains endlessness hereafter.
Free of possessiveness, free of ego, free of hope, equal everywhere, desireless and unstruck: this is the eternal dharma of the good.
Trust, modesty, endurance, renunciation, purity, alertness, absence of cruelty, freedom from delusion, compassion toward beings, absence of slander,
gladness, contentment, wonder, humility, good conduct, calm, purity of action, good understanding, release,
equanimity, celibacy, complete renunciation, freedom from possessiveness, freedom from hope, a dharma not to be bought:
gift without return, sacrifice without return, study without return, vow without return, acceptance without return, dharma without return, austerity without return.
These are called "upward-streaming": the gods are held to be transformations; they transform by nature, having reached heaven here and there; whatever they wish, all that they enjoy and distribute.
This is the conduct of goodness told to you, best of brahmins; having known it by rule, one gains whatever he wishes.
The qualities of goodness have been told especially, and the conduct of the qualities duly told. The man who always knows these qualities enjoys the qualities and is not enjoyed by them.
They attach to one another, live on one another, depend on one another and follow one another.
As long as there is goodness there is darkness, without doubt; as long as there is darkness and goodness, so long, it is said, there is passion.
Joined, they make their course together, moving in groups; these live in aggregates, by reasons and non-reasons.
Of these, mutually turning in surplus and deficiency, it goes on, as there is less or more, in everything.
Where darkness is in surplus and has gone to animal state, passion should be known as small there, and goodness still smaller.
Where passion is in surplus and has gone to the middle stream, darkness should be known as small there, and goodness still smaller.
Where goodness is in surplus and has gone to the upward stream, passion should be known as small there, and darkness still smaller.
Goodness is the transformation, the womb, the illuminator of the senses; no other state higher than goodness is ordained.
Darkness in the shudra, passion in the kshatriya, goodness in the brahmin the best: so the three qualities turn in the three classes.
Even from afar they are seen together, moving in groups; darkness, goodness and passion have not been heard of as separate.
At the sight of the rising sun, fear arises for bad thieves, and travellers are tormented, afflicted by thirst and suffering.
The sun is said to be goodness, the bad thieves darkness, and the travellers' torment is called the passionate quality.
In the sun, illumination is goodness, heat is the passionate quality, and the eclipse of it at the new and full moon should be known as dark.
So in all lights the three qualities turn, and go on in succession here and there as they do.
In immovable beings darkness has gone to animal state; the passionate turn about, and a state of affection is goodness.
The day should be known as threefold, the night is ordained threefold; the fortnights, months, years, seasons and junctures likewise.
Gifts are given threefold, sacrifice proceeds threefold, the worlds are threefold, the Vedas threefold, the sciences threefold, the goals threefold.
Past, future and present, dharma, wealth and desire, prana, apana and udana: these are the three qualities.
Whatever there is in this world, all of it is in these systems; the three qualities go on unmanifest always; goodness, passion and darkness are the eternal creation of the qualities.
Darkness is the unmanifest, auspicious, eternal, unborn, the eternal womb; nature, modification, dissolution, Pradhana, origin and end.
Unsurging, undiminished, unshaking, unmoving, firm, being and non-being: all that is held the unmanifest of three qualities. Its names are to be known by men who contemplate the Self.

One who truly knows the names of the unmanifest and the qualities, all the paths and the only ones, freed from body, knowing the truth of division, is freed from all the qualities and free of ailment.
The great Self is described by words that are synonyms; the wise brahmin who knows it does not come to delusion.
With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads and mouths everywhere, with hearing everywhere in the world, it stands pervading all.
The Person of great light and flame, lodged in the heart of all, minuteness, lightness, attainment, lordship, imperishable light:
there are the worlds of the wise, of those devoted to renunciation, the meditators, constant yogis, true to their promises and masters of their senses,
and some who are learned, free of greed, anger conquered, calm of mind, steadfast, without possessiveness or ego: all these, freed, attain greatness.
The steadfast one who knows the holy highest goal of the great Self does not come to delusion in all worlds; Vishnu himself becomes the lord, self-existent, in the first creations.
The man who thus knows the lord who rests in the cave, the ancient Person of universal form, golden, the highest goal of the wise, the wise one stands beyond understanding.
Beings are bewildered in the five great elements, in sound, touch, form, taste, smell and action.
At the end of the destruction of the great elements, when dissolution has come, great fear arises, steadfast one, for all who bear life.
If a being is born from something, it dissolves back into it; they dissolve in reverse order and are born in succeeding order.
Then when all beings, immovable and moving, are dissolved, the steadfast, remembering, are never dissolved.
Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as fifth, joined with action and cause, are impermanent, called delusion.
Joined with greed and procreation, without distinction, owning nothing, masses of flesh and blood, living on one another,
they are called external selves, wretched, of miserable conduct. Prana, apana, udana, samana and vyana,
these five winds are called the inner self; with speech, mind and intellect, they make the world eight-fold.
Other undifferentiated things are joined with action. In both, the mind is to be known, and the intellect is the twelfth.
These eleven senses have been told by me in order; the wise, knowing them, think "it is done".
Beings have three places; a fourth does not occur: land, water and sky; birth too is fourfold.
Egg-born, sprouting, sweat-born and womb-born: this fourfold birth is marked for the whole host of beings.
Know the immovable beings, and also those that move in the air, as egg-born, and all creeping things too.
Sweat-born are said to be worms and such creatures; this second birth is called the lowest.
Beings that are born, at the turn of time, by splitting the earth, best of brahmins, are called sprouts.
Two-footed and many-footed beings, and those going across, know them, good ones, to be womb-born.
The eternal womb of Brahman is to be known as twofold here: austerity and action, which is merit; so is the view of the wise.
Action is to be known as twofold: sacrifice and giving at the sacrifice; and study by one who is born is merit: so say the aged.
One who knows this by rule, best of brahmins, would be a chief; and learn this too: that he is freed from all sins.
Space is the first element; hearing is its spiritual aspect, sound its elemental aspect, the directions its divine aspect.
The second element is wind; skin is its spiritual aspect, the touchable its elemental, lightning its divine aspect.
The third they call light; the eye is the spiritual aspect, form the elemental, the sun the divine aspect.
The fourth is to be known as water; the tongue is the spiritual aspect, taste the elemental here, the moon the divine aspect.
Earth is the fifth element; the nose is the spiritual aspect, smell the elemental, wind the divine aspect.
This is the fourfold rule among the five elements. Next I shall tell all the senses, threefold.
Brahmins who see reality say the feet are the spiritual aspect; the elemental is what is to be gone to, and Vishnu the divine aspect.
The downward-going apana and the anus are the spiritual aspect; discharge is the elemental, Mitra the divine aspect.
The generative organ of all beings is called the spiritual aspect; semen the elemental, and Prajapati the deity.
Those who know the spiritual call the hands the spiritual aspect; actions are the elemental, Shakra the divine aspect.
The Vaishvadevi, with mind first, speech is here called the spiritual; the speakable is elemental, and Fire the divine aspect.
They call the mind spiritual, following the five elements; the thinkable is elemental, and the Moon the divine aspect.
They call the intellect spiritual, moving among the six senses; the knowable is elemental, and Brahma the divine aspect.
This rule of the spiritual has been told to you by me truly; knowledge of it, knowers of dharma, is gained here by the wise.
The senses, the objects of the senses and the five great elements: one should reflect on all these, joining them with the mind.
When the whole mind is exhausted, birth is not sought for happiness; that is the happiness the wise hold for those whose goodness is endowed with knowledge.
Next I shall tell the auspicious withdrawal from all beings that makes for subtle states, by gentle or by harsh means.
Without attachment to qualities or non-qualities, a solitary course follows; they say this conduct from the brahmin is the one-step happiness.
The learned man who withdraws all desires from everywhere, like a tortoise its limbs, free of passion, freed everywhere, is always happy.
Restraining desires in the self, with thirst exhausted, composed, a friend of all beings, kindly, he goes to Brahman-hood.
By restraint of all the senses that seek objects and by the sage's abandoning of the settled country, the spiritual fire is kindled.
As a fire kindled by fuel shines with great light, so by restraint of the senses the great Self shines.
When, serene in self, he sees beings in the heart of the self, self-originated, he then attains the subtlest of the subtle, unsurpassed.
Fire is form, water is the stream, wind is touch, earth is the terrible bearer of mud, and space is hearing.
Filled with passion and grief, covered by five streams, joined with the five elements, nine-doored, with two deities,
menstruating, unseen, threefold and of three constituents, delighting in contact, deluded: this is the notion of the body.
Hard to move in the world of the living, it depends on goodness; and in this world the wheel of time turns.
This terrible, fathomless great ocean called delusion should be let go, drawn in, and awakened with the gods in the world.
By restraint of the senses he gives up desire, anger, fear, delusion, malice and falsehood, so hard to give up.
One who in the world has conquered these, the three qualities and five elements, has his supreme, endless place seen in space.
Having crossed the river with desire as its bank, endless, a stream of mind, terrible, a pool hard to pass, he conquers both desire and anger.
Freed from all faults, he then sees the Highest; placing the mind in the mind, he sees the Self in the Self.
The all-knowing one looks at the Self in the Self in all beings, transforming himself in one way and in many, here and there.
He surely sees forms, as a hundred lamps from one lamp; he is Vishnu, Mitra, Varuna, Fire, Prajapati.
He is the Establisher and the Ordainer, the lord facing every way; the great Self shines in the heart of all beings.
Hosts of brahmins, gods and asuras, yakshas, pishachas, ancestors, birds, hosts of rakshasas and spirits, and great sages always praise him.
The sheep among all animals, the mouse among those who dwell in holes, the bull among cows, and the man among women.
Banyan, rose-apple, the vishvaka, pipal, silk-cotton, shimshapa, meshashringa, kichaka and bamboo: these are the kings of trees in this world, without doubt.
Himavan, Pariyatra, Sadya, Vindhya, Trikutavan, Shveta, Nila, Bhasa and the mountain Kashthavan,
Shubhaskandha, Mahendra and the mountain Malyavan: these are the kings of mountains, and the Maruts of the hosts.
The Sun is lord of the planets, the Moon of the stars, Yama lord of the ancestors, the Ocean of the rivers.
Varuna is king of the waters, Mitra is called the lord of beings, the Sun is lord of the hot, and the Moon is called lord of the lights.
Fire is always lord of beings, Brihaspati of brahmins, Soma lord of herbs, Vishnu the best of the mighty.
Tvashtri is sovereign of forms, Shiva lord of animals, sacrifice of gifts, and the sages of the Vedas.
Know the goddess Uma as the best and fairest of women; the Earth among delights, and the apsarases among women.
Kings are devoted to dharma, brahmins marked by dharma; therefore a king should strive here to protect the twice-born.
In the realms of kings where the good languish, those kings are lacking in all their own virtues and go downward after death.
Those in whose kings' realms the good are well protected rejoice in this world and hereafter attain endlessness; know this, best of brahmins, great souls.
Now I shall tell the fixed mark of dharma: dharma is marked by non-harm, and harm is the mark of adharma.
The gods are marked by illumination, men by action; space is marked by sound, and wind by touch.
The mark of lights is form, and waters are marked by taste; earth, the supporter of all beings, is marked by smell.
Speech, refined by vowels and consonants, is marked by truth; the mark of mind is thought, and so is the intellect, by connection.
Thinking of objects with the mind, one then determines with the intellect; the intellect is surely marked by determination.
The great is marked by meditation, the unmanifest by goodness, yoga by activity, and knowledge is marked by renunciation.
Therefore, putting knowledge first, the wise should renounce here; the renouncer joined with knowledge attains the highest goal. Passing beyond dualities, he goes beyond darkness, death and old age.
The dharma joined with its marks has been told to you by me duly. Next I shall rightly tell the grasping of the qualities.
The quality of earth, smell, is grasped here by the nose; and the wind in the nose is ordained for the knowledge of smell.
The element of water, taste, is always grasped by the tongue; and Soma in the tongue is ordained for the knowledge of taste.
The quality of light, form, is grasped by the eye; and the Sun in the eye is ordained for the knowledge of form.
The quality of wind, touch, is known by the skin; and Wind in the skin is ordained for the knowledge of touch.
The quality of space, sound, is grasped by the ear; and the directions in the ear are proclaimed for the knowledge of sound.
The quality of mind, thought, is grasped by wisdom; the element of consciousness in the heart is ordained for the knowledge of the mind.
The intellect, by determination, and the great, by meditation, grasp always by certainty the unmanifest, without doubt.
The knower of the field, which is without mark, which is eternal and of the nature of no qualities, grasps without a mark; therefore the knower of the field is without mark, marked only by knowledge.
The unmanifest is declared the field, the origin and dissolution of the qualities. I always see, know and hear it dissolved.
The Person knows it; therefore he is called the knower of the field; the knower of the field looks on the whole conduct of the qualities.
From beginning through middle to end, what is being created is insentient; the qualities do not know the Self, being created again and again.
No one knows truth; only the knower of the field finds what is beyond the qualities, the great one beyond the qualities that are the quality-becoming.
Therefore, giving up the qualities and the principle here, the knower of truth, his faults exhausted, having left the qualities, enters the knower of the field.
Free of dualities, without saying "mine", without svadha, motionless and homeless, the knower of the field is the supreme lord.
Day comes first, then night; the months begin with the bright fortnight, the asterisms with Shravishtha, the seasons with winter.
Earth is the first of smells, waters of tastes, light of forms, and wind is called the first of touches; space is the first of sound: this is the quality made by the elements.
Now I shall tell the best first of beings: the Sun is the first of lights, and Fire is held the first of elements.
Savitri is first of all sciences, Prajapati of the gods, Om of all Vedas and of words, prana: whatever in the world is fixed in it is all called Savitra.
Gayatri is the first of metres, the goat is called first of animals, the cow of quadrupeds, and the twice-born of men.
The hawk is first of birds, the oblation the best of sacrifices, and the serpent, best of brahmins, the eldest of all reptiles.
The Krita age is the first of all the ages, without doubt; gold of all jewels, and barley of herbs.
Of all foods and drinks, grain is called the highest; of all liquids and drinks, water is the best.
Of mountains the great Meru is held the eldest of all; of directions and intermediate directions, the upward direction was born first.
So Ganga of the three paths is held the eldest of rivers, and of all lakes and waters the ocean is the eldest.
Of gods, danavas, beings, pishachas, serpents, rakshasas, men, kinnaras and yakshas, the lord is the master of all.
Vishnu, made of Brahman, is the beginning of the whole universe; there is no higher being than him in the three worlds.
Of the stages of life, the householder's is chief of all, without doubt; the unmanifest is the beginning of the worlds, and the end of all is that same.
Days end in sunset and night ends in sunrise; the end of pleasure is always pain, and the end of pain is always pleasure.
All accumulations end in exhaustion, all elevations in falling, all unions in separation, and life in death.
Everything made ends in destruction, death is certain for the born; all this, moving and unmoving, is impermanent in this world.
Sacrifice, gift, austerity, study, vows and rules all end in destruction; there is no end to knowledge.
Therefore, with pure knowledge, serene of soul, composed, free of possessiveness and ego, one is freed from all sins.
Entered by old age and grief, moving among disease and calamity, reflecting on place and time, with the sound of toil and exertion,
encircled by day and night, circled with cold and heat, painful with the ends of pleasure and pain, pegged by hunger and thirst,
scored by shade and sun, agitated by blinking, thronged with people of terrible delusion, existing yet insentient,
reckoned by fortnights and months, an uneven wandering through the world, a mud of heaps of darkness, driving the force of passion,
blazing with the ornament of goodness, a circle of the aggregate of qualities, with the navel of voices and bodies, turning with grief,
joined with action and cause, extended with passion, counted by greed and desire, born of distinct knowledge,
surrounded by fear and delusion, causing bewilderment of beings, with a support of joy and love, taking desire and anger,
ending from the great to the particulars, arising unattached and imperishable, swift as thought, tireless, the wheel of time turns.
One who always knows truly the course and the withdrawal of the wheel of time does not become bewildered among beings.
Freed from all distress, passing beyond all dualities, the sage, freed from all sins, attains the highest goal.
Householder, celibate student, forest-dweller and mendicant: the four stages are declared, all with the householder's as root.
Whatever tradition is proclaimed in this world, going to its end is best; this is the eternal fame.
Refined by rites earlier, having properly practised his vows, the Veda-knower should return in a birth distinguished by qualities.
Delighting in his own wife, self-controlled, of good conduct, master of senses, with faith, he should sacrifice with the five great sacrifices.
Eating what remains after gods and guests, devoted to Vedic rites, joined with sacrifice and giving, as able and as the rule requires.
A sage is not restless in hands and feet, nor restless in eyes, nor in speech or limbs: this is the range of the cultured.
He should always wear the sacred thread of sacrifice, wear white, keep pure vows, be restrained by self-control and giving, and always associate with the cultured.
Master of sex and belly, friendly, composed in cultured conduct, he should carry a bamboo staff and a water-pot.
Having studied he should teach, and sacrifice and officiate, give and receive: he should follow a livelihood of six kinds.
The three actions that are the brahmins' livelihood here are officiating, teaching, and accepting from the pure.
How that may be protected, dear one, son of Pandu, the kingdom and dharma, you know, son of Kunti; learn that.
I, in some holy place, keeping a vow, shall do my time at once, along with the wise Rama.
The best of men entered the abode of Mahendra and of the wise Kubera, and the worlds of Varuna.
